ops.title: Scheduler poll gating, outage/recovery sweep, and the streak ledger
ops.body:
Rationale extracted from the daemon scheduler + server during the 2026-07 comment diet. Source keeps terse contracts; the design detail lives here.

## pollGated — why needs-login needs its own clock
pollGated reports whether an account is backed off so pollOnce skips it with no network attempt (and it never serves as the outage canary). Two independent backoff clocks:
- a recent rate-limit sample still inside its exponential backoff (rlBackoff over the acct 429 streak), and
- a needs-login / exhausted-auth-streak account inside the needs-login interval.
The needs-login backoff needs its OWN clock because a 401 inserts no usage sample, so it cannot ride the rate-limit backoff (which keys off the latest usage-sample timestamp). Store I/O runs outside ledMu; the streak reads take ledMu only around the bookkeeping.

## pollAccount — recovery sweep and refresh-token double-spend safety
pollAccount samples one account and reports the outcome for outage detection. Caller holds the poll claim, has cleared the backoff gates (pollGated), and owns inter-account spacing.
`recovery` forces AllowBusyRefresh for a busy account regardless of the auth streak — the post-outage heal. This stays safe because fetchUsage's deep guard (post-401 + provably-expired + credential-unchanged re-read) still prevents a refresh-token double-spend; the streak gate is only a heuristic layer on top.

## The prior-401 accepted gap (pollAccount body)
The prior-401 gate gives a lazily-waking session one full poll to self-refresh first. Accepted gap: a busy, clock-fresh, server-revoked token keeps 401ing (fetchUsage's busy guard requires expiry), so needs-login waits for clock expiry — the live session owns recovery; refreshing sooner could double-spend a refresh token it still needs. A recovery sweep bypasses the streak gate (fetchUsage's deep guard still holds) so a busy account whose token expired during the outage heals now.

## pollAccounts — snapshot skip conditions (history)
pollAccounts is the per-account sweep (the account.poll row). It reports whether the poll completed cleanly so a status snapshot should be written: false on every skip-the-snapshot condition (ctx cancellation, list-accounts failure, a still-down outage canary, or entering/re-entering outage). Each of these was historically a bare `return` in the old monolithic pollOnce; the status.snapshot row is the last poll row, so stopping the table there reproduces the old snapshot skip exactly.

## server.go — the shared self-heal ledger (led / ledMu)
`led` is the self-heal ledger store shared by every ported Server-owned family: the fp.domain and fuse.remount rows, plus the auth.streak and ratelimit.acct / ratelimit.pool streaks. (The holder cache's fuse.deepwedge / fuse.shallowdead rows live in holderState.led under its own mu.)
ledMu is the enclosing serialization the `ledgers` type documents: rows are touched from the heal tick, the scheduler poll loop, and the select/status/repair RPC handlers plus migrate/strand/convert — so every s.led access takes ledMu, never held across mount/Sync/re-register/bounce or usage-fetch/refresh I/O (bookkeeping in, I/O out).
History: the streaks were scheduler-goroutine-local (no lock) before the fold onto the ledger substrate; sharing one map with the concurrently-touched heal-family rows makes ledMu mandatory on every streak access too.

## select.go — last-good-sample vs. 429 placeholders
Status utilization, resets, timestamp, and overage source from the last GOOD sample, not samples[0]: a 429 poll records a zeroed `rate_limited` placeholder as the newest row (load-bearing for daemon backoff — pollGated keys off it), so samples[0] would read 0%/no-overage for a rate-limited account. HasUsage gates on that known-good sample too, not on any sample: an account whose only rows are 429 placeholders has no real utilization, so ok=false is no-data (status renders "no data", not "0% used"). The newest-row RateLimited flag is still tracked separately.
ops.when: editing the daemon scheduler's poll backoff gates (pollGated, poolRateLimited, pollAccount), the outage/recovery-sweep logic, or the shared self-heal ledger (s.led / ledMu) and its auth/ratelimit streak rows
